reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the key premises of improved CO oxidation activity, the specific 63% T10 reduction, and enhanced durability for the 7-metal vs 4-metal spinel, but it does not provide evidence for the claimed mechanism (oxygen mobility/Mars–van Krevelen) or explicitly demonstrate reduced precious metal dependence, leaving two premises unsupported.
premises: Increasing configurational disorder in spinel oxides by incorporating multiple first-row transition metals enhances CO oxidation activity
The 7-metal spinel oxide shows a 63% decrease in T10 for CO oxidation compared to a 4-metal variant
The 7-metal spinel oxide exhibits superior long-term stability (4.7% vs 12.2% deactivation over 14 h)
The enhanced performance is due to improved lattice oxygen mobility and activation via a Mars–van Krevelen mechanism
This approach reduces dependence on precious metals by improving the support material
